mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 110 Octa engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Land Rover Defender 110 Octa (S68) engine typically costs between £8,000 and £14,000 for supply only, with fully rebuilt options ranging from £12,000 to £18,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbocharger or cooling failure in a Land Rover Defender 110 Octa?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs include unexplained coolant loss, a distinct sweet smell from the engine bay, or reduced boost pressure under heavy acceleration.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 110 Octa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the exceptional retained value of the L663 Defender 110 Octa (typically £150,000-£180,000+), a rebuild is highly financially viable.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 110 Octa engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for the Land Rover Defender 110 Octa typically takes 3 to 5 days due to the complexity of the L663 chassis and twin-turbo MHEV electrical architecture.

mainEntity.name: Can the S68 engine in the Land Rover Defender 110 Octa be upgraded for better reliability during replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many specialists recommend upgrading to revised coolant crossover pipes and improved turbocharger seals during an S68 replacement.

problems.rootCause: The "hot-vee" twin-turbo layout generates extreme under-bonnet temperatures, placing significant thermal stress on coolant crossover pipes, turbocharger seals, and high-pressure fuel components over time.
